_comment: The executed operating point. Read by environment/bia_corpus.py, and through it by bia_loader.py, bia_harness.py, gpt.py and the verifier's evaluator. ONE declaration; nothing downstream restates a number from here.

gradeable._state: MEASURED in this bundle's own verifier image on one H100 80GB. Per full max_schedule_steps run: 108 s of training and 45 s of held-out evaluation, and the verifier makes three such runs -- the handed anchor probe, the refined anchor probe and the submission -- so the graded run lands near 460 s. The bound point below could not be graded at all: the slot last ran 1987 s and returned a constant zero.
gradeable._target_loss_note: 6.22 is CHOSEN BY MEASUREMENT, not by authoring. The held-out curves of the two verifier probes were measured at this point on the verifier's own split, at the bound eval_stride of 20, and 6.22 is the bar at which the two ends of the reward scale are furthest apart in STEPS while still leaving sustain_points further scheduled points inside max_schedule_steps for the later of them. Measured: the handed recipe reaches 6.2292 at step 260 and 6.2475 at 240; the refined probe reaches 6.2100 at 220 and 6.2378 at 200. Every one of those sits at least 0.009 from the bar, against a re-run reproducibility of 0.0003 measured by running the handed recipe twice.

bound._state: The upstream nanogpt speedrun point this slot was authored against. Retained and selectable with BIA_OPERATING_POINT=bound so the re-scale below can be checked against it rather than trusted. It is NOT gradeable: measured, one optimizer step of this configuration plus its thirty 500 MB snapshots and their held-out evaluations does not finish inside any grading budget in this corpus.
